slides.title: First Permanent Embodied AI Entertainment Experience Launches in Europe
slides.highlight: This launch highlights the growing integration of embodied AI in public entertainment spaces, offering insights relevant to the development of socially engaging embodied robots like Haru.

slides.title: EZRA Launches Loop: Connected Human and AI Coaching
slides.highlight: The launch of Loop by EZRA represents a connected human and AI coaching experience, which parallels MOSAIC's focus on adaptive AI coaching to enhance human proficiency.

slides.title: FraudSociety: A Generative Agent-Based Society for the Financial-Fraud Economy
slides.highlight: This work introduces FraudSociety, an LLM-agent-based simulator that jointly models informational and financial dynamics to study large-scale fraud, offering a scalable testbed for evaluating anti-fraud interventions.

card.one_liner: FraudSociety jointly models informational and financial dynamics in fraud via LLM agents and persistent ledgers.
card.key_idea: Integrates dynamic social graphs, persistent financial ledgers, and a Need-Intent-Action architecture to couple information exposure with financial outcomes.
card.evaluation: Validated against FTC/CAFC statistics using Quartet Distance; reproduces loss concentration and tests five counter-fraud interventions.
card.limitation: Relies on LLM decision-making fidelity and small-scale simulation (112 civilians) which may limit generalizability to larger populations.

slides.title: Realbotix Launches Echo Humanoid Robot Line
slides.highlight: Realbotix has launched the Echo humanoid robot line, featuring tabletop and full-body models designed for social engagement, which aligns with HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception in human-AI interactions.

slides.title: Simulation-Efficient Double-Flow Neural Posterior Estimation for Agent-Based Models
slides.highlight: This work introduces Double-Flow Neural Posterior Estimation (DF-NPE), a method that significantly reduces the computational cost of Bayesian inference in agent-based models by combining learned summaries with synthetic data generation. It is relevant to MIMIC as it offers a scalable approach for parameter estimation in complex multi-scale simulations of hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: DF-NPE reduces agent-based model simulation costs by 90% using synthetic data from learned summaries.
card.key_idea: Combines a recurrent encoder for time-series summaries with two normalizing flows: one generates synthetic latent data, the other estimates the posterior.
card.evaluation: Tested on Brock-Hommes asset-pricing model using Wasserstein distance and MMD against likelihood-based MCMC ground truths.
card.limitation: Performance depends heavily on the allocation ratio between direct and synthetic data and the specific training strategy chosen.

slides.title: Multimodal Socially Aware Framework for Human-Robot Interaction in Virtual Reality
slides.highlight: This study evaluates a multimodal framework integrating speech, vision, and touch for robot social interaction in VR, identifying gaps in autonomous performance compared to teleoperation.

card.one_liner: A multimodal framework integrating speech, vision, and touch for socially aware robot behavior in VR.
card.key_idea: Uses a VLM to process speech, vision, and touch inputs, generating coordinated robot actions and speech via interaction history.
card.evaluation: 18 participants in VR across five scenarios; autonomous system rated above neutral but significantly lower than teleoperated baseline.
card.limitation: High response latency (3.7s) and lack of clarification strategies caused breakdowns; results limited to VR simulation.

slides.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning of Co-Adaptive Hip Exoskeleton Control (MARL-Exo) for Metabolic Energy Reduction
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework where an exoskeleton policy co-adapts with a musculoskeletal human model in simulation, achieving significant metabolic energy reduction in real users without per-user tuning.

card.one_liner: Simulated co-adaptive RL policy reduces exoskeleton metabolic cost in humans without per-user tuning.
card.key_idea: Multi-agent RL co-adapts a full-body musculoskeletal model and hip exoskeleton using physiological metabolic energy rewards.
card.evaluation: Validated on eight adults via indirect calorimetry; showed 18.3% reduction vs passive and 7.4% vs no-exo, though high variance.
card.limitation: High inter-subject variability (up to 24.2% benefit) and reliance on simulation fidelity for transfer to diverse real-world users.

slides.title: Improving Group Deliberation through AI-Guided Self-Reflection
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that AI-guided self-reflection improves group deliberation quality and empathy toward dissenting peers, offering insights relevant to ADAM-CHAT's goal of fostering aligned, adaptive human-AI teaming through meta-cognitive scaffolding.

card.one_liner: AI-guided self-reflection significantly improves subsequent group deliberation quality compared to static reflection or no reflection.
card.key_idea: Participants engage with a non-directive AI chatbot for structured self-reflection before joining synchronous, anonymous three-person group discussions on policy topics.
card.evaluation: Randomized experiment (N=1,173) using Discourse Quality Index and psychometric surveys; results show moderate effect sizes (d≈0.3) and are statistically robust.
card.limitation: All group members shared the same condition, limiting real-world applicability where reflection participation is heterogeneous among peers.

slides.title: Agent-Based Transport Model Calibration via Online Stochastic Batch Optimization
slides.highlight: This work introduces an online calibration framework for agent-based models that reduces computational burden by estimating parameters within a single simulation run, relevant to MIMIC's need for efficient meso-scale simulation of hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Calibrates agent-based transport models within a single simulation run using online stochastic batch optimization.
card.key_idea: Embeds parameter updates into MATSim iterations by treating replanning agents as stochastic batches, enabling co-evolution of parameters and behavior.
card.evaluation: Validated on a large-scale Swiss transport scenario; mode shares aligned with observed data within a typical simulation timeframe.
card.limitation: Relies on a quasi-static assumption that choice variables remain stable between iterations, which may not hold in highly dynamic networks.

slides.title: Context-Aware Generation and Modulation of Expressive Motion Behavior using Multimodal Foundation Models
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates how multimodal foundation models can generate context-aware, expressive full-body gestures for robots, directly supporting the development of engaging embodied social interactions.

card.one_liner: Generates context-aware, expressive robot motion using multimodal foundation models and knowledge distillation for low latency.
card.key_idea: Uses DMPs to modulate gestures via Principles of Animation, guided by distilled multimodal LLMs for real-time, cross-morphology control.
card.evaluation: User study (30 participants) on Pepper robot showed better context alignment than baselines; validated latency via distillation and versatility on other robots.
card.limitation: Depends on pre-recorded gesture libraries and specific robot kinematic descriptions; distillation requires large training datasets for effective latency reduction.

slides.title: EvolveMAS: A Unified Self-Evolution Framework for Decentralized Multi-Agent Systems
slides.highlight: EvolveMAS introduces a unified framework for test-time adaptation and experience reuse in decentralized multi-agent systems, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's goal of AI teammates that adapt beyond in-context learning and self-correct via meta-cognition.

card.one_liner: EvolveMAS enables decentralized multi-agent self-evolution via external memory governance across diverse interaction settings.
card.key_idea: Pairs agents with dedicated MemoryAgents to maintain structured memory, enabling within-episode adaptation and cross-episode knowledge reuse without parameter updates.
card.evaluation: Tested on five benchmarks (cooperative, mixed-motive, adversarial); achieves 77.2 average score, outperforming baselines by 9.7 points with validated ablations.
card.limitation: Relies on external MemoryAgents for governance, potentially increasing computational overhead and complexity compared to self-managed memory approaches.

slides.title: Realbotix Launches Echo Humanoid Robot Line
slides.highlight: Realbotix has launched the Echo humanoid robot line, introducing new commercial platforms for embodied social interaction.

slides.title: Beyond Aggregate WER: In-domain Adaptation, Learner Speech, Code-Switching, and Speaker Attribution in Online Spanish Learning Classrooms
slides.tldr: IN-DOMAIN ADAPTATION FOR BILINGUAL CLASSROOM ASR
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that domain-matched adaptation significantly improves speaker attribution and recognition of code-switched learner speech, addressing critical challenges in multimodal social perception of hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: In-domain LoRA adaptation of MOSS rivals commercial ASR for bilingual Spanish classrooms, outperforming Whisper.
card.key_idea: LoRA adaptation on small in-domain classroom data significantly improves MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize, surpassing Whisper and matching commercial Muse.
card.evaluation: Six ASR systems tested on seven held-out sessions using WER, CER, and DER, disaggregated by speaker role and language context.
card.limitation: Small dataset (seven evaluation sessions) from one institution; results may not generalize to other contexts or larger corpora.

slides.title: When Does GenAI Use Support Critical Thinking? A Cross-Cultural Structural Account of Transactive Memory with GenAI
slides.tldr: STRUCTURAL TMS ACCOUNT OF GENAI CRITICAL THINKING
slides.highlight: This study extends Transactive Memory Systems theory to human-AI partnerships, identifying that critical thinking in GenAI-assisted work depends on coordinating cognitive labor and reworking outputs rather than mere exposure, offering a structural framework relevant to modeling hybrid team dynamics.

card.one_liner: Structural engagement, not exposure, determines if GenAI supports critical thinking across cultures.
card.key_idea: Transactive Memory Systems theory applied to human-AI partnerships, modeling how familiarity, confidence, and reflective transformation predict critical thinking enactment.
card.evaluation: Survey of 891 US and Turkish students using structural equation modeling; results show largely invariant cross-cultural structure with minor exceptions.
card.limitation: Cross-sectional correlational design limits causal inference; reliance on self-reported binary outcome and convenience sampling introduces potential bias.

slides.title: Metacognitive Decoding: Efficient Inference for Diffusion Language Agents
slides.highlight: This work introduces a metacognitive controller for diffusion language agents that dynamically adapts token generation and computation based on environmental interaction, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and efficient test-time adaptation.

card.one_liner: Metacognitive controller reduces diffusion agent inference FLOPs by 20.6% while maintaining accuracy.
card.key_idea: Lightweight controller guides decoding via confidence alignment for structural tokens and flux policy to shrink active computation ranges.
card.evaluation: Tested on five benchmarks (BFCL, HotpotQA, etc.) against diffusion baselines; shows significant FLOP reduction with competitive accuracy.
card.limitation: Controller adaptation to evolving diffusion models remains an open challenge for future work.

slides.title: Disparity Laundering: Consensus Without Fairness in Clinical Multi-Agent Systems
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that consensus mechanisms in clinical multi-agent systems can obscure rather than eliminate demographic bias, a finding critical for MIMIC's goal of ensuring fairness in hybrid human-AI societal simulations.

card.one_liner: Clinical multi-agent systems launder demographic bias into consensus, requiring diverse-perspective ensembles for repair.
card.key_idea: Agents share bias but never compare counterfactuals; a diverse-perspective ensemble makes disparity visible internally to neutralize it.
card.evaluation: Tested on 120 MIMIC-IV-ED cases across five models and four topologies using counterfactual demographic swaps and triage gaps.
card.limitation: Limited to 120 cases and binary sex/race axes; relies on structured decision schemas rather than free-text reasoning.

slides.title: Select-TTT: Query-Conditioned Selective Fast Weight Updates for In-Place Test-Time Training
slides.tldr: QUERY-CONDITIONED FAST WEIGHT UPDATES FOR TTT
slides.highlight: This paper introduces Select-TTT, a method that improves test-time training by scaling fast-weight updates based on query relevance, addressing the dilution of relevant information in long-context tasks. This approach is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's goal of enabling AI teammates to adapt at test time and maintain alignment with evolving user intents in long-horizon agentic tasks.

card.one_liner: Select-TTT improves long-context QA by scaling fast-weight updates based on query relevance.
card.key_idea: Modulates In-Place TTT chunk updates with query-conditioned multipliers derived from frozen LM head logits.
card.evaluation: Tested on LongMemEval-S and LoCoMo with Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-4B; outperforms uniform In-Place TTT baselines.
card.limitation: Relies on frozen output head for relevance scoring, which may be noisy or misaligned for complex queries.

slides.title: GARDEN: Generalist Autonomous Reward Design Through Evidence Navigation for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
slides.highlight: GARDEN uses LLMs to autonomously design reusable reward functions for cooperative multi-agent teams, directly supporting ADAM-CHAT's goal of adaptive AI teammates that align with evolving team goals in benchmarks like Overcooked-AI.

card.one_liner: GARDEN uses LLMs to design transferable reward functions for cooperative multi-agent tasks via autonomous evidence navigation.
card.key_idea: An LLM engineer autonomously inspects code, artifacts, and behavior to generate a single reward program, tested via probes and selected by a fixed rule.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on Overcooked and SMAX held-out scenarios; GARDEN outperformed native shaping and fixed-diagnostic baselines with significant win-rate gains.
card.limitation: High computational cost due to extensive LLM calls and token usage; generalization is limited to related task families with shared mechanics.

slides.title: Exploring AI Peer in Collaborative Mathematics Learning
slides.tldr: AI PEER PERCEPTION IN MATH LEARNING
slides.highlight: This study identifies design dimensions for AI peer agents, such as tentative reasoning and non-judgmental interaction, that foster collaborative learning. These insights inform the development of adaptive AI coaching systems within MOSAIC's coadaptive loop.

card.one_liner: Experts perceive AI as a peer through social behaviors like shared control and imperfection, not just mathematical competence.
card.key_idea: An adaptive LLM agent combining Big Five persona embeddings with motivational state modulation to simulate peer-like collaborative reasoning.
card.evaluation: Thematic analysis of interviews with seven domain experts interacting with the agent; qualitative insights rather than quantitative learning gains.
card.limitation: Small sample of experts (not students) and reliance on a single prototype architecture limits generalizability to real-world educational settings.

slides.title: Beyond Utterance-Level Speaker Similarity: Perception-Aligned Segmental Evaluation of Accent in Speech Generation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a segmental evaluation protocol for accent in generated speech, revealing that local perceptual evidence can yield different system rankings than global similarity scores. It is relevant to HyECHO for understanding how fine-grained acoustic features influence social perception and identity recognition in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: Segmental accent evaluation reveals pronunciation differences missed by utterance-level similarity scores.
card.key_idea: Protocol combining speaker/accent SMOS with subword annotations from target-region listeners to locate perceived accent differences.
card.evaluation: 47 listeners rated 200 pairs from Scottish/Australian voices; seven objective metrics showed weak correlation with segmental annotations.
card.limitation: Modest inter-annotator agreement and limited speaker/sample size due to budget constraints require further validation.

slides.title: Making Sense of Audience Change: Causal Attribution and Boundary Management on Xiaohongshu
slides.tldr: CAUSAL ATTRIBUTION AND BOUNDARY MANAGEMENT IN SOCIAL PLATFORMS
slides.highlight: This study examines how users attribute community changes and manage boundaries on recommendation-driven platforms, offering insights into social perception dynamics relevant to modeling hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: Users attribute community change to algorithms or social actors, linking these explanations to specific boundary management strategies.
card.key_idea: Thematic and quantitative analysis of Xiaohongshu comments links causal attributions (algorithmic vs. social) to boundary strategies (technical vs. social).
card.evaluation: Analyzed 262 comments from eight threads via thematic coding and permutation tests; strong association (Cramér’s V = .583) between attribution and strategy.
card.limitation: Small, purposive sample of public comments from a single event; association does not establish causality or generalizability.

slides.title: Behavioural Quality Is Not Learning Utility: Objective Mismatch in Human Behaviour Models for Robot Learning
slides.tldr: BEHAVIORAL FIDELITY DOES NOT PREDICT RL TRAINING UTILITY
slides.highlight: This paper demonstrates that human behavior models evaluated for high fidelity to real data may not provide optimal training signals for reinforcement learning policies, a finding directly relevant to RwB's focus on AI-mediated embodied learning and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Human behaviour model realism does not consistently predict downstream RL policy performance in HRI tasks.
card.key_idea: Compare generative model metrics (FD, KL) against RL policy returns across driving and handover domains using diverse trajectory representations.
card.evaluation: Tested rule-based and data-driven models on highD and handover@RPL datasets, correlating metrics with Deep Q-Learning performance.
card.limitation: Findings may not generalize to all HRI tasks; results are sensitive to specific trajectory representation choices.
